posts.title: the ai kitchen
posts.linkedin:
poteto talking about agents as a kitchen team was one of my favorite parts of her interview with matt pocock.

you give the team what they need, organize the work, and check what gets served. you're still responsible for the result.

i liked how concrete that made it. worth watching if you're figuring out how to work with agents too.

posts.title: give agents hands and eyes
posts.linkedin:
this part of matt pocock's interview with poteto gave me some ideas for my own setup.

give the agent a way to run the app, use it, and see what happened. screenshots and traces help it figure out where things went wrong.

i came away thinking about what my agents can actually check for themselves.

posts.title: how the agents coordinate
posts.linkedin:
i liked hearing poteto explain how she coordinates agents in her interview with matt pocock.

she teaches them where to find context, then uses coordinator agents to delegate and follow up.

that gave me a few ideas about the time spent explaining the same things over and over. really enjoyed this interview.

posts.title: merging while sleeping
posts.linkedin:
poteto lets her agents merge code while she sleeps. hearing her explain it to matt pocock made me curious about how she got comfortable with that.

she built up verification, reviews the commits in the morning, and changes the rules when something goes wrong.

i learned a lot from this interview. worth watching for the details behind her setup.
